title: What Carpentry Is
description: Signature framing: the Signature shop treats every build as a measured plan first, with the cut list written before any saw starts. The Signature edition of this build uses its own dimensions, 26 x 4 x 1 inches (W x H x D), and its own cut list below. This is a Signature original design, labeled signature-original, and it is not presented as an authentic public record.

image.description: Original dimensioned project sketch for What Carpentry Is: a front-view diagram showing the overall 26 x 4 x 1 inch (W x H x D) form, the main cut pieces, and the overall dimensions labeled on the drawing, drawn for this record.
image.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" role="img" aria-label="What Carpentry Is"><rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" fill="#f7f2e8"/><rect x="30" y="40" width="340" height="52" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="30" y1="40" x2="370" y2="92" stroke="#333"/><text x="30" y="25" font-size="13">What Carpentry Is</text><text x="30" y="100" font-size="12">Overall 26 x 4 x 1 in (W x H x D)</text><text x="30" y="290" font-size="11">Original dimensioned project sketch: front view with cut pieces shown below.</text><rect x="40" y="110" width="120" height="10" fill="none" stroke="#555"/></svg>

specs.dimensions: 26 x 4 x 1 in (W x H x D)
fasteners: No fasteners for this overview; practice joints use wood glue and 1-1/4 in screws
specs.tolerances: Cut to within 1/16 in; check square by measuring both diagonals and matching them.
specs.load_notes: A practice board carries no load; it is for learning cuts and joints.
specs.arithmetic_note: Cut list adds up: Total pieces: 1 (1 x Practice board). Longest piece 26 in fits within the 26.3059 in face diagonal of the overall form. Cut the longest pieces first so a mistake on a short piece does not waste a long board.

steps: Read the cut list and the arithmetic note in full, and check every piece against the plan; measure twice before cutting.
Cut the pieces in order, longest first: Practice board (26 x 4 x 0.75 in).
Dry-fit the frame without glue and check both diagonals match so the assembly is square.
Carpentry is the craft of cutting, joining, and finishing wood into useful things, from a simple box to a staircase.
Glue and fasten as listed in the specs, keeping the assembly square while fasteners go in; wipe glue squeeze-out before it dries.
Sand through the grits, ease the edges, and finish as described in the record; check the finished piece for square and for its rated load before use.

safety_gear: Work gloves for handling rough lumber (never near rotating blades)
tools.safety_notes: Wear eye protection for every cut and sanding pass, hearing protection for power tools, and a dust mask for sanding. Unplug power tools or remove batteries before changing blades or bits, keep guards in place, and keep hands clear of blades. Clamp work before cutting, never hold a small piece by hand near a blade, and clear offcuts before the next cut.

demo.code:
PIECES = []
PIECES.append(('Practice board', 26.0, 4.0, 0.75, 1))
print("Board-foot estimate: What Carpentry Is")
total_bf = 0.0
for name, L, Wd, T, qty in PIECES:
    bf = L * Wd * T / 144.0 * qty
    total_bf += bf
    print("%s: %.2f board feet" % (name, bf))
print("Total board feet: %.2f" % total_bf)
print("With 10%% waste allowance: %.2f board feet" % (total_bf * 1.10))
print("Total pieces: %d" % 1)
demo.expected_output:
Board-foot estimate: What Carpentry Is
Practice board: 0.54 board feet
Total board feet: 0.54
With 10% waste allowance: 0.60 board feet
Total pieces: 1

specs.dimensions: 50 x 24 x 2 in (W x H x D)
fasteners: Wood glue and 2 in screws, 24 total
specs.tolerances: Cut to within 1/16 in; check square by measuring both diagonals and matching them.
specs.load_notes: A sample frame holds about 60 pounds in testing.
specs.arithmetic_note: Cut list adds up: Total pieces: 8 (2 x Frame rail, long, 2 x Frame rail, short, 4 x Leg). Longest piece 50 in fits within the 55.4617 in face diagonal of the overall form. Cut the longest pieces first so a mistake on a short piece does not waste a long board.

steps: Read the cut list and the arithmetic note in full, and check every piece against the plan; measure twice before cutting.
Cut the pieces in order, longest first: Frame rail, long (50 x 4 x 0.75 in), Frame rail, short (24 x 4 x 0.75 in), Leg (24 x 1.5 x 1.5 in).
Dry-fit the frame without glue and check both diagonals match so the assembly is square.

The family framework is the ladder the whole suite climbs: simple builds use straight cuts and butt joints, compounded builds add a joint or a curve, and complex builds combine joints, angles, and fitted parts.
Glue and fasten as listed in the specs, keeping the assembly square while fasteners go in; wipe glue squeeze-out before it dries.
Sand through the grits, ease the edges, and finish as described in the record; check the finished piece for square and for its rated load before use.

safety_gear: Work gloves for handling rough lumber (never near rotating blades)
tools.safety_notes: Wear eye protection for every cut and sanding pass, hearing protection for power tools, and a dust mask for sanding. Unplug power tools or remove batteries before changing blades or bits, keep guards in place, and keep hands clear of blades. Clamp work before cutting, never hold a small piece by hand near a blade, and clear offcuts before the next cut.
